newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sacked Mexican general denies drug corruption.
newsitem.headline: Sacked Mexican general denies drug corruption.

text.p: Mexico's top anti-drug official, jailed on corruption charges, has admitted knowing a drug henchman but said he made the contact hoping it would lead to the arrest of a cocaine king, newspapers reported on Friday.

The newspapers said Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, fired on Monday after two months as head of the National Institute for Drug Combat (INCD), had pleaded innocent in an initial statement to prosecutors.

Gutierrez Rebollo's arrest provoked the most serious drug corruption scandal ever made public in Mexico and triggered rebukes from Washington, where officials worry that secret drug intelligence shared with the general may now be in cartel hands.

The government ordered Gutierrez Rebollo and two aides to be imprisoned after alleging they had taken payoffs from the country's top drug lord Amado Carrillo Fuentes, nicknamed "The Lord of the Skies", in return for information and protection.

In his statement read to local media on Thursday, Gutierrez Rebollo admitted contacts with Jose Eduardo Gonzalez Quirarte, a presumed lieutenant of Carrillo Fuentes, the newspapers Reforma and El Universal reported.

El Universal quoted the general's testimony as saying that "for one and a half years (he) knew of the links that existed between Gonzalez Quirarte and the drug trafficker known as 'The Lord of the Skies', for this reason, with authorisation of his superiors, he kept up the relationship in order to obtain important information to fight drug trafficking and arrest Carrillo Fuentes".
The Attorney-General's office refused to provide texts of the testimony or to comment on its content Friday.
Reforma also said Gutierrez Rebollo had declined to make any further statement on Thursday in court until he had been allowed to hire a lawyer.

Two of his aides arrested with him, Horacio Montenegro and Javier Garcia, both alleged in statements that they had been tortured for four days in a Mexico City army base to testify against the general.
